goal: Investigate model mismatch within a bounded thermal experiment budget.

revision_semantics.register_revision: Stage a provisional fitted candidate for testing, not acceptance or causal identification.
revision_semantics.confirmation: To test a fitted candidate: register_revision first, then propose_experiment on its returned model_id with kind confirmation.
revision_semantics.verdict: Only measured confirmation supports or rejects a staged revision on that tested input.

decision.rationale: Compare bounded predictive candidates numerically before spending physical experiments; initial-0, initial-1, initial-2 cover joint heating and single-sided heating. Fitting is not causal confirmation.

Training fits on initial-0, initial-1, initial-2 favor linear by BIC but fitting is not independent confirmation; propose diagnostic sustained-both to independently test initial model at higher sustained temperature where quadratic loss would diverge.

result.note: Explicit preparation and dispatch through Investigation are required

decision.rationale: Compare bounded predictive candidates numerically before spending scarce experiments; re-fit linear on initial-0, initial-1, initial-2 plus action-2 sustained-both which showed no_mismatch_observed (probe_rmse 0.0768). Fitting is not causal confirmation.

Linear fit on initial-0, initial-1, initial-2 plus action-2 sustained-both has best BIC so far, and action-2 showed no_mismatch_observed (probe_rmse 0.0768c), but fitting is not independent confirmation nor mechanism. Sensor_lag and quadratic_loss have only been fit on initial-0,1,2; compare quadratic_loss numerically on the same full evidence including high-temperature sustained action-2 before spending scarce experiments (3 actions left, 5 fits left).

Linear fit on action-2+initial-0,1,2 has best BIC (-2429.7) and probe RMSE 0.0768 with no_mismatch_observed on action-2, quadratic_loss on same evidence is worse (-2417.4) with near-zero quadratic terms, but sensor_lag has only been fit on initial-0,1,2. Compare sensor_lag numerically on same full evidence before spending scarce experiments. Fitting is not confirmation.
